title: Extract a 5378-series terminal with a single HT60630B blade
objective: Hold the compatible housing with its locking tab upward, bend the wire down, insert one HT60630B blade beneath the locking tab, and pull the wire and tool together to remove the terminal.
skills: single-blade insertion beneath a recessed tab
coordinated same-direction tool and wire pull
success_conditions: The selected 5378 terminal exits its cavity through robot-applied blade and pulling forces while the housing remains intact and no neighboring terminal is released. Zero for bypassing the locking tab, wire/crimp separation, housing damage, unintended extraction, or state overwrite. Exact force and damage thresholds remain blocked pending measurements.
industrial_value: Molex provides an explicit manufacturer procedure for extracting individual 5378 terminals with this tool, establishing a real connector-service operation.
dexterity: High. Unlike the selected dual-blade process, this sequence requires wire bending, insertion of one blade beneath a specific tab, and simultaneous withdrawal of the wire and tool.

evidence.quote: Individual terminals may be extracted from the housing using this tool.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series

evidence.quote: Hold the housing with the locking tab facing up. Bend the wire down and insert one of the blades of the extraction tool into the housing under the locking tab.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series, step 1

evidence.quote: Hold the wire against the extraction tool and gently pull the terminal by the wire and the extraction tool at the same time out from the housing in the direction shown.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series, step 2

asset_plan: Acquire the authoritative 5378 housing and terminal drawings and reference hardware before modeling. Use rigid PhysX geometry and an articulated locking tab calibrated from the actual parts. Validate wire-bending clearance, tab release, simultaneous pull, damage modes, and YAM reachability before full-demo work.
risk: Not selected. It is meaningfully different in contact mechanics from the dual-blade 5556 procedure, but the acquired package lacks a 5378 housing drawing, selected part number, complete geometry, and robot-application evidence. It also shares the broader depinning objective, so it offers weaker novelty separation than the selected, better-specified four-circuit Mini-Fit Jr. setup.
